full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiffs in brief is that, one Abdus Subhan was the owner of the land described in the plot No. 15 including plot No. 16 and plot No. 14. The predecessor of the plaintiffs sheik Dengu alias Dengu Haji became the owner and possessor of the aforesaid land by way of purchase from Abdus Subhan. Gul Mamod, son of Abdus Subhan, died leaving his son Rashid Ullah and subsequently by amicable partition Lal Mamod and Lebus Ullah amicably partitioned the suit land whereby Lal Mamod got 11 Ana 8 Pai and Lebus Ullah got 5 Ana 4 Pai. By successive transfer the plaintiffs Nos. 1-4 got the suit land by way of purchase. In the survey and settlement operation the name of Lebus Ullah was correctly recorded but plot No. 14 and 16 was wrongly recorded in the name of the Government. In the above premise the predecessor of the plaintiff Nos. 1-10 and plaintiff Nos. 11-14 instituted Title Suit No. 132 of 1985 before the then Munsef, Baniyachong for declaration of title and obtained decree on 29.03.1986. The predecessor of the plaintiffs No. 1-10 instituted another Title Suit being No. 62 of 1987 for declaration of title and for injunction in respect of the land stated in 2nd schedule and obtained decree on 18.09.1988. Earlier the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 211 of 1961 for recovery of khas possession and after getting decree on 05.02.1966 got possession through execution case No. 75 of 1966. The plaintiffs on getting decree filed mutation Case No. 41 of 2001 to the office of the defendant No. 4 for the correction of record of right which was sent to defendant No.1 for final- approval but after elapse of long time no step was taken for disposal of the mutation case and as such the plaintiffs are constrained to file the suit seeking mandatory injunction. 

 9. Having gone through the pleadings, evidence and other material on record, it appears that the plaintiffs earlier of decrees their favour for declaration or title and recovery of khas possession and by filing execution case got delivery of possession. Although, the Government in the pleadings stated that they will take legal steps challenging those decrees but till date no step has been taken to this end. So, a decree whether exparte or contested has got sanctity until and unless such decrees are set aside, altered or varied.
